key_insight: Calibrated XGBoost performed best among the evaluated models for retrospectively identifying a composite of documented suicide-related outcomes in an age-matched EHR cohort.
clinical_relevance: The framework highlights clinical and social-contextual information that may support future suicide-risk research, but it does not establish readiness for clinical screening.
method: Grouped MIMIC-IV diagnosis codes into clinically motivated features and a composite suicide-related outcome.
Retained all positive patients and sampled age-matched comparison patients to address imbalance and age confounding.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost with isotonic calibration and SHAP interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used retrospective MIMIC-IV EHR data before and after age-matched resampling; the abstract reports strongest matched-cohort performance for calibrated XGBoost without numerical metrics.
watch_item: Code-based outcomes may miss undocumented events, and performance in an age-matched cohort may not translate to prospective risk prediction in routine populations.
paper_title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
